The development phase of the proposed Integrated Management Information System for the Tricycle Franchising and Regulatory Office (TFRO) of Lucena City will focus on translating the approved system design into a functional web-based application that supports franchise processing, operator and driver profiling, violation monitoring, payment recording, and report generation.

The researchers will develop the system using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript as the primary technologies for building the structure, layout, and interactive components of the system interface. The system will be coded and managed using Visual Studio Code (VS Code) as the development environment to ensure organized and efficient program implementation. Prior to actual system development, the interface layout and system prototype design will be created using Figma to visualize system structure and improve usability planning.

For database management and system integration, Firebase will be utilized to support real-time data storage, authentication services, and secure record management of franchise applications, operator and driver information, violation records, and administrative reports. Firebase authentication features will also be used to implement role-based system access for authorized TFRO personnel.

The system will include essential modules such as franchise registration and renewal management, operator profiling, driver profiling, violation monitoring, payment tracking, and automated report generation. Validation controls and user-access restrictions will be incorporated throughout the system to ensure accuracy, reliability, and protection of sensitive regulatory data. Continuous refinement will be conducted during development to ensure alignment with the operational workflow of the Tricycle Franchising and Regulatory Office of Lucena City.
The developed Integrated Management Information System will undergo Black Box Testing to verify whether the system performs according to its specified functional
requirements. This testing method will evaluate the correctness of system outputs based on user inputs without examining the internal structure of the program.

Each major system module, including franchise processing, operator profiling, driver profiling, violation monitoring, payment recording, and report generation, will be tested individually and collectively to ensure proper functionality and integration. Test cases will be prepared for each module, and testing results will be recorded as either pass or fail based on expected system behavior.

Errors and inconsistencies identified during testing will be documented and corrected immediately to improve system performance and operational reliability. Selected technical evaluators with knowledge in information systems will participate in the testing process to ensure that the system functions effectively prior to deployment for user evaluation.

Through this testing procedure, the researchers will ensure that the developed system meets the functional requirements necessary to support the regulatory services of the Tricycle Franchising and Regulatory Office of Lucena City.
